newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE OPPOSITION TRIAL DELAYED UNTIL FRIDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE OPPOSITION TRIAL DELAYED UNTIL FRIDAY.

text.p: A Harare court has delayed until Friday its ruling on a request by veteran Zimbabwean opposition leader Ndabaningi Sithole for a postponement of his trial on charges of plotting to assassinate President Robert Mugabe.
Court officials gave no reasons for the postponement and Sithole's lawyers were unavailable for comment.

Sithole asked High Court Judge James Devittie last week to postpone his trial, saying he had been given little time to prepare his defence and also wanted to challenge the constitutionality of one law under which he is charged.
His lawyer, Tendai Biti, told the court he was only given the final prosecution documents on October 30, three days before the scheduled November 4 trial start.
Sithole, 77, is facing charges of illegal arms possession, involvement in acts of sabotage and terrorism and conspiracy to murder Mugabe, his political rival for over 30 years.
